concepts.def: Molecule (usually protein) on a pathogen surface that triggers an immune response.
Engulfing of pathogens by phagocytes; vesicle fuses with lysosome to digest the pathogen.
Recognises antigens presented on APCs, releases cytokines to stimulate B cells and cytotoxic T cells.
Lymphocyte that, when activated, divides and differentiates into plasma cells producing antibodies.
Y-shaped glycoprotein with variable region complementary to a specific antigen; agglutinates pathogens.
Long-lived lymphocyte produced after primary response, enabling rapid secondary response on re-infection.
